'''Michael Girard''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Gold 120 from Apache Junction, Az. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run. At DecipherCon 1999 Michael also played [[Young Jedi]]: finished 45 in YJ Qualifier #2 (Sealed Deck).<ref name="dc99yj02_2">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ02_2.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: YJ Qualifier #2 (Sealed Deck)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010108185300/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ02_2.html Internet Archive]</ref>

He started playing in Great Falls, Montana, winning a sealed-deck demo tournament run by [[James Lafferty]]. He qualified for the 1998 World Championships, where he played eventual champion [[Matt Potter]]. He was Gold 120 in the Tatooine region, from Apache Junction, AZ.<ref name="decsq-prof">[http://www.decipher.com/volunteers/squadrons/players/girardmichael.html Star Wars CCG Squadrons: Gold 120 profile], decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000604073410/http://decipher.com:80/volunteers/squadrons/players/girardmichael.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Other sourced notes ==

Gold 120, Apache Junction, Arizona. Named in Warren Holland's 25 January 2002 Players' Committee announcement as the first Player Advocate for Player Support.

The anagram list unscrambles [[Caldera Righim]] as Michael Girard.

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Girard playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001).
